foundation: Barrot V3 execution, verification and safety
key_findings: Coinbase officially offers USDC loans powered by Morpho on Base and lists XRP as eligible collateral up to $100,000.
Coinbase's cbXRP is a Base wrapper backed 1:1 by XRP in Coinbase custody; Coinbase says the underlying is not sold, transferred or utilized by Coinbase.
Morpho Watch reports a candidate cbXRP/USDC Base market with 118.55M cbXRP collateral, $59.2M USDC borrowed and 90.4% utilization, but the exact mapping to Coinbase retail loans is unconfirmed.

The candidate market has a 62.5% LLTV while Coinbase's generic loan page says 86% LTV; market positions exceed Coinbase's $100,000 retail XRP borrow cap. These are disconfirming signals against treating the entire market as Coinbase's retail loan book.

Circle and Coinbase remain economically intertwined: Coinbase renewed its Circle arrangement on the same terms and reported all-time-high USDC balances; Circle disclosed substantial distribution costs to Coinbase.

Coinbase's Q3 2026 filing shows $306.9M stablecoin revenue and 59%/53% YoY declines in consumer/institutional spot volume, supporting a strategic shift toward stablecoins, payments, derivatives, prediction markets and onchain activity.
Coinbase added RLUSD on XRPL, Base and Ethereum on October 28; Global Exchange collateral use was announced as future, not yet live.
SBI Holdings, not Tokyo SBIC, is the connective corporate node between Ripple and Circle: Ripple shareholding/JV, Circle investment/JV, USDC/RLUSD distribution, Arc validator.
Tokyo SBIC is the Tokyo Small and Medium Business Investment & Consultation Co., Ltd.; its June 2025 ChatGPT course was training for investee companies, not a partnership.
The Camilla Stephenson identity remains unresolved; a Dr. Kamilah/Camila Stevenson candidate is plausible but not verified, and a full public-video inventory is incomplete.
